title: The New Playbook for Companion Screen Advertising | Genius Sports
summary: The Companion Screen offers new research revealing how the relationship between television and mobile is reshaping sports advertising.
body_markdown:
*Seven in ten weekly sports viewers want personalized advertising, while six in ten want ads relevant to what is happening in the game*


- 59% of weekly sports viewers want advertising tied to what is happening live in the game
- 71% want advertising personalized to their interests
- Scores, big plays, halftime and breaks are among the moments when fans are most receptive to advertising
- 61% would welcome a personalized mobile offer connected to an ad they just saw on TV


**NEW YORK, August 31, 2026** — Genius Sports (NYSE: GENI), a global leader in real-time sports data and technology, today released


*The Companion Screen: A New Era of Sports Consumption and Advertising,* new research revealing how the relationship between television and mobile is reshaping sports advertising.


Marketers have traditionally approached television and mobile as separate environments that accompany different media strategies, ad creative and measurement. However, sports fans do not experience those screens as separate environments, but rather as a cohesive experience in which each screen has a role in enhancing the entire sports experience.


While watching a game, mobile has become an indispensable companion to television and the overall sports consumption experience: a place to message friends, check scores and stats, browse social media for additional insights and commentary on the game, shop and engage more deeply with what is happening on screen. Genius Sports’ new thought leadership research shows that this creates an opportunity for advertisers to think beyond simply reaching the same fan across multiple devices and instead


connect the experience across


screens, to both the individual fan and the specific moments unfolding in the game.


Among people who watch sports at least weekly, 71% want mobile advertising personalized to their interests and 59% want advertising personalized to what is happening in the game they are watching.


The next era of sports advertising goes beyond targeting the right fan or even the right game. It is about understanding what is happening in the game in real time and aligning advertising with the mood and momentum of the fan experience. A big play, a tense finish or a break in the action creates a different mindset — and a different opportunity for brands to connect. Fans identified halftime (30%), their team scoring or making a big play (29%), and close or exciting moments (23%) among the moments when relevant advertising can have the greatest impact.


“Mobile is no longer a ‘second screen’; it’s the companion screen, helping fans connect, react to the game in real time and engage with brands in relevant ways,” said Tony Marlow, Chief Marketing Officer at Genius Sports. “Everything happening around the game, from social and fantasy to prediction markets and live experiences is turning up the surround sound of sports. The game is getting bigger, more connected, and more immersive. And fans are telling us exactly what they want from brands in that environment: to connect the experience across screens and make every interaction relevant to both who they are and what’s happening in the game.”


The research points to a new model for sports advertising that brings three signals together:


who the fan is, what is happening in the game


and which screen they are using. The opportunity extends across screens, with 61% of weekly sports viewers saying they would welcome a personalized mobile offer connected to an ad they had just seen on TV.


Genius Sports enables this through its


Fan Graph


and


Moment Engine


. The Fan Graph brings together fan identity,


interests


and behaviors to help brands understand who they are reaching, while the Moment Engine uses proprietary live sports data to identify and


activate against


meaningful moments as games unfold. Together, they enable marketers to reach the


right fan, on the right screen, at the right moment.


Genius Sports fielded the survey among


1,001 U.S. adults during the week of August 10, 2026


, with results balanced to U.S. Census figures for age, gender,


income and region.


The full report,


The Companion Screen: A New Era of Sports Consumption and Advertising, is


[available here](https://digital.geniussports.com/l/822433/2026-08-28/tztlrj) .
